fields.description:
In _(public/)lib/classes/files/curl_security_helper.php,_ the call order check in _get_resolve_info()_ closes the _empty()_ check brackets in the wrong place, which should be corrected.

This does not appear to introduce any obvious security issues because all core flows perform the correct calling order, but this should be fixed on all security supported versions to avoid accidentally introducing any security risks / bypassing any checks in the future.

*Update:* Unit testing the corrected IF statement also uncovered that there were a couple of use cases where the previous implementation worked unexpectedly (threw an exception and rejected the request), because we assumed the hosts, IPs and ports would always be set, and assumed those not being set meant the correct execution order was not performed to check the cURL security config. This was not always true, because some of those values will not be set in cases where no cURL security settings are configured on the site (and therefore no limitations apply). This surfaced since these appear to not be set by default in unit testing.

fields.description:
In [MDL-69877] a new security.txt file, following the information @ [security.txt|https://securitytxt.org/] was introduced.

The security.txt file located in _public/security.txt (or security.txt pre 5.1)_ must be updated regularly, shortly before it expires (defined by the {{Expires}} element within the file).

+*The updates should be made to main, as well as all other security supported Moodle versions that contain security.txt.*+ This means all supported versions have an identical security.txt file (including the same expiry).

This task must only land in the minor release versions that are scheduled for release alongside the relevant major release  (for example if 5.3 is the major release, then 5.2.3 will be one of the minors receiving the update, assuming no unscheduled releases have bumped it to 5.2.4 already). Therefore, the ideal window for landing this issue is +2-6 weeks prior to release+.

As a minimum, this will involve updating the {{Expires}} value, which needs to be set to *[expected subsequent major release date]* *+ 3 WEEKS*. This provides a small buffer in case the major release is delayed. If any of other details in the security.txt need to be amended, they should also be completed at the same time. We should also check the RFC in case of any changes (see the [Github repo|https://github.com/securitytxt/security-txt] to check if any versions have been released since the previous LMS release).

----

Detailed information (to be modified for each clone of this issue):

* *Branches affected:* main (5.3), 5.2, 5.1, 5.0, 4.5
* *Expiry (6.0 release + 3 weeks):* 19 April 2027 + 3 week = 10 May 2027
* *Commit message:* MDL-XXXXXX core: Update security.txt expiry
* *Other changes:* _... add any further changes required here_

Exact formatted expiry date to use: *2027-05-10T01:00:00.000Z*

How the date format was calculated (in line with the [latest spec|https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9116#name-expires] - RFC 9116):

{{date --date='10 May 2027 01:00' -u +"%FT%H:%M:%S.000Z"}}

----

(This issue is part of the release process, 2 weeks before release, and will be cloned as part of it.)

issuetype.description: A task that needs to be completed.  Tasks usually refer to work that must be done outside the product. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)

components.name: LTI External tool
components.description: Bugs and improvements related to LTI External tools (previously named 'External tool')

fields.description:
This issue is scoped with decoupling the ltixservice_toolsettings plugin from mod_lti.

Analysis of this plugin shows:

* There are 3 contexts (not moodle contexts) which settings service calls operate at for get/set: site, context and link (and each is represented by a class in toolsettings/classes/local/resources/). Only link is currently ties to instanceid  - its file is linksettings.php.
* \core_ltix\helper::set_tool_settings() and \core_ltix\helper::get_tool_settings() are used by all three to get/set the settings values, but with varying optional params, depending on whether it's site, context or link settings.
** The third param is link id the instance dependency .
** Only link settings requires using the linkid param, whereas the other two (site settings, context settings) do not.

*linksettings.php:*

* linksettings::execute():
** reads from the lti table, should read from resource link via the repository/manager.
** passes lti->course to helper::get_tool_settings() and helper::set_tool_settings(). I.e. for existing tools, when link settings are to be set, a course was historically passed.
*** Now, we'll need to find the course from the resourcelink's context, via something like:
{noformat}$courseid = null;
$coursecontext = \core\context::instance_by_id($link->get('contextid'))->get_course_context(false);
if ($coursecontext) {
   $courseid = $coursecontext->instanceid;
}{noformat}
*** If a link resides outside a course, that's already handled via the above code, without erroring. 
* linksettings::parse_val() - used during launch, to resolve custom parameter value for $LtiLink.custom.url. Will need to be updated.
** see linkmemberships.php in the memberships service code for an example of how to get the link from the launchcontext and use the linkid. e.g. use:
{noformat}$resourcelink = $launchcontext->get(resource_link_context::class)->resourcelink;
$this->params['link_id'] = $resourcelink->get('id');{noformat}
*  instead of using cm->instance for the value of $this->params['link_id'].

*helper.php (not service plugin code but these methods are only used by this service + should be in scope here):*

* the helper methods ::get_tool_settings and set_tool_settings should be changed to take linkid as the final param, instead of instanceid.

*lib/db/install.xml + upgrade code:*

* lti_tool_settings definition should be updated so that 'coursemoduleid' reads 'resourcelinkid'
** Note: coursemoduleid isn't even historically accurate, since it wasn't the cmid actually being stored; it was the cm->instance. Since, for upgrading sites, all links are mapped to the same ids as the lti instances they originated from/relate to, no data fix is needed. The table already has instance recorded, and this value will be mapped to the links already. 
**  We therefore just need the table column name change in install + an upgrade step to fix the table column name for existing sites.

Since this will likely be worked on after [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-81864|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-81864|smart-link] is completed, we should confirm whether the backup and restore of the tool settings needs to be handled as part of this issue (last we checked, Shamim did have code handling that in the backup issue)

{{Ungültiger Rückgabewert: Invalid external api response: the value is "<think>Okay, the user greeted me in French with "Bonjour gerda, ca va?" which means "Hello Gerda, how are you?" The (local) server it is querying is running a OpenWebUI instance which provides an "OpenAI API compatible chat completion endpoint".
I was unable to find out if this a violation of the OpenAI API schema (in that case I'll gladly pester someone else with a bug report in a more relevant project) or something that could happen with the models available at OpenAI as well (I don't use AI outside the locally hosted models at work).

fields.summary: Single quotes in search query return no results on MSSQL (non full-text fallback path)

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
h3. Summary

When using the Simple search engine ({{search_simpledb}}) on a site where {{is_fulltext_search_supported()}} returns false (e.g. MSSQL without full-text search installed), searching for a term containing a single quote (e.g. it's) returns no results.

!Screenshot 2026-04-13 at 18-37-50 Global search int_nftss.png|width=250!

Single quotes

!Screenshot 2026-04-13 at 18-38-04 Global search int_nftss.png|width=250!

Double quotes

h3. Root Cause

In {{search/engine/simpledb/classes/engine.php}}, the {{get_simple_query()}} method only strips double quotes from the query string before building the LIKE-based SQL:

{noformat}$q = str_replace('"', '', $q);{noformat}

Single quotes are left untouched, which causes the LIKE '%it's%' parameter to effectively break on MSSQL, silently returning no results.

h3. Steps to Reproduce

# Set up a Moodle site on MSSQL without full-text search enabled
# Enable global search with Simple search engine
# Index some content
# Search for a term containing a single quote (e.g. it's or Moodle's)
# Observe: no results returned

h3. Expected Behaviour

Search results containing the term should be returned, with the single quote either stripped or properly handled.

h3. Suggested Fix

In get_simple_query(), also strip single quotes:

{noformat}> $q = str_replace(['"', "'"], '', $q);{noformat}

fields.summary: Add Moodle 5.2.0 upgrade line to all the upgrade.php scripts

issuetype.description: A task that needs to be completed.  Tasks usually refer to work that must be done outside the product. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)
issuetype.name: Task

fields.description:
To have it properly detected for the future, it would be great to add to all the upgrade.php scripts some lines like these:

{code:php}// Automatically generated Moodle v5.2.0 release upgrade line.
// Put any upgrade step following this.{code}

exactly before the "{{return true;}}" present in all the scripts.

Normally, it's ok to do that both in the stable (502_STABLE) and the {{main}} branches, so they will allow quickly find where 5.2.0 started and act once we decide future requirements.

But, *when under parallel development, this only can be done in the stable (502_STABLE) branch* as the {{main}} branch already has diverged and can have own upgrade steps not corresponding to the version just released, but to the future version being developed in parallel.

The change can be performed globally with:

{code:java}#!/bin/bash
export rel="5.2.0" && find . -name upgrade.php | \
xargs grep -l 'function.*xmldb_.*_upgrade' | \
grep '/db/' | \
xargs grep -L "Automatically generated Moodle v${rel} release upgrade" | \
xargs perl -p -i -e 's@( *)(return true;)@\1// Automatically generated Moodle v$ENV{rel} release upgrade line.\n\1// Put any upgrade step following this.\n\n\1\2@s'{code}

*Command to detect* all the upgrade.php files not having those lines:

{code:java}find . -name upgrade.php | xargs grep -l 'function.*xmldb_.*_upgrade' | grep '/db/' | xargs grep -L 'Automatically generated Moodle v5.2.0 release upgrade'{code}

*Commands to detect* that we have not added the lines to incorrect files:

{code:java}grep -lr 'Automatically generated Moodle v5.2.0 release upgrade' * | grep -v '/db/'
grep -lr 'Automatically generated Moodle v5.2.0 release upgrade' * | xargs grep -L 'function.*xmldb_.*_upgrade'{code}

*Command to detect* if the lines have been added after a post-release upgrade step. If there are upgrade steps found, verify that all of them were already there the day of the release and have not been introduced later (you can look for differences between the release v5.2.0 and the current {{main}} branch to verify that)

{code:java}export rel="5.2.0" && export ver="202604" &&
find . -name upgrade.php | \
xargs grep -B25 "Automatically generated Moodle v${rel} release upgrade" | \
grep "upgrade_.*_savepoint.*${ver}"{code}

*Important note to integrators*: The sooner this issue is integrated after release, the fewer chances to get the lines put in an incorrect place (that's what the last "command to detect" above tries to avoid. We need to ensure that the lines are *exactly* at the release point (or we may end up deleting upgrade steps incorrectly in the future). So, immediate integration after release (within the on-sync period and ideally before any new upgrade step is added), it the best achievement.

Ciao 🙂

h3. Summary

Create the User Interface for the OAuth2 Server user authorisation workflow. This covers three screens, plus a refactor to share common logic between them.

This is UI/rendering work only. Wiring these screens into the actual OAuth2 authorisation route/controller (parent epic MDL-87215) is out of scope here.

There is no existing UX/Figma mockup to follow. Visual design should follow the existing login page's style and components, reusing the same page layout/branding (site logo, background, language menu, maintenance banner) for all three screens so the flow feels consistent.

h3. Screens

*1. Login screen (existing, to be updated)*

* This is today's Moodle login screen ({{core_auth\output\login}}), shown when the user isn't already logged in.
* It should additionally display the requesting OAuth2 client's identity (name, logo/icon, link to the client's website) so the user knows what they're logging in for _before_ entering credentials.

*2. "Continue as [user]" screen (new)*

* Shown when the user is already logged in.
* Displays the current user's name and profile picture, and asks them to confirm they want to continue as that user.
* Displays the requesting client's identity (name, logo/icon, link to website) for the same trust/verification reasons as the login screen.
* Includes a "Not you? Log in as a different user" option, which logs the current user out and shows the login screen instead.

*3. Scope confirmation screen (new)*

* Lists the scopes being requested, each with a brief description.
* Where the client has previously been granted some scopes by this user and is now requesting more, the screen distinguishes between:
** _Already granted_ scopes (shown informationally)
** _Newly requested_ scopes (require the user's consent)
* Displays the requesting client's identity (name, logo/icon, link to website).
* Approval is _all-or-nothing_ — the user cannot selectively approve/deny individual scopes. They either approve the full set of newly-requested scopes, or cancel.

h3. Shared behaviour across all screens

* *Decline/Cancel*: clicking Cancel/Deny on the continue-as-user or scope-confirmation screen redirects back to the client's {{redirect_uri}} with a standard OAuth2 {{error=access_denied}} response, per spec. No Moodle-side "access denied" page.
* *Silent re-authorisation*: if a logged-in user re-authorises a client for scopes they've already fully granted (no new scopes requested), the continue-as-user and scope-confirmation screens should be skipped — but the current user's name and profile image should still be shown briefly/contextually as part of that flow, so it's clear who is continuing.
* Shared rendering logic (error/info messages, maintenance banner, language menu, etc.) currently embedded in {{core_auth\output\login}} should be extracted into a reusable trait so it can be shared across the login, continue-as-user, and scope-confirmation renderables without duplication.

h3. Out of scope / not included

* Behat acceptance test coverage — not currently feasible to validate an OAuth2 flow end-to-end in Behat; test coverage will need to be addressed separately (e.g. via unit/JS tests where practical).
* Wiring these renderables into the OAuth2 authorisation route/controller (tracked under the parent epic/other tickets).

h3. Notes

A proof-of-concept branch exists (MDL-87215-main) with a rough sketch of a shared {{login_renderable_trait}} and {{core_auth\output\oauth2\confirm_scopes}} / {{continue_as_user}} renderables. This PoC is exploratory only and does _not_ represent the agreed design — it should inform, not dictate, the implementation of this ticket.

fields.description:
Develop endpoints and backend logic to allow revocation of access tokens, authorization codes, and refresh tokens. Ensure revocation is immediate and properly invalidates tokens across the system.

h2. Approach

Implement a single, unified {{/revoke}} endpoint per RFC 7009 (OAuth 2.0 Token Revocation), rather than separate endpoints per token type. The endpoint accepts {{token}} and {{token_type_hint}} parameters and always returns HTTP 200, even for already-invalid or unknown tokens, to avoid leaking token validity to attackers.

h2. Authentication & authorization

* Confidential clients must authenticate to call {{/revoke}}.
* Public clients are not required to authenticate, but the token being revoked must be verified as belonging to the calling {{client_id}} before it is revoked (prevents a client revoking another client's token).

h2. Cascading revocation

* Revoking a refresh token must cascade: all access tokens issued from that refresh token are invalidated in the same operation, fully cutting off the client's access.
* Revoking an access token or authorization code only invalidates that specific token.

h2. Enforcement mechanism

Because access tokens may be JWTs (stateless), a revocation/denylist table must be maintained and checked on every authenticated API request so that revocation takes effect immediately, rather than relying on short token lifetimes alone.

h2. Scope boundaries

* In scope: the client-facing {{/revoke}} endpoint and its backend revocation logic (self-service revocation by the token owner).
* Out of scope: admin-initiated bulk revocation UI/flows (e.g. an admin revoking all tokens for a user or client) — this belongs to the OAuth2 Server administration UI tickets (MDL-88468, MDL-88474), which can call into this backend logic later.

h2. Dependencies

* *Blocked by MDL-89181* (Implement OAuth2 Server client manager class) — needed to resolve/validate the client_id and enforce token-ownership checks for public clients.
* *Related to MDL-89089* (Implement OAuth2 Server Scope repository layer) — in progress; not a hard blocker, but scopes tied to revoked tokens should be considered during implementation.

h2. Acceptance criteria

# {{/revoke}} endpoint implemented per RFC 7009 semantics (always 200, {{token}} + {{token_type_hint}} params).
# Client authentication enforced for confidential clients; token-ownership verified for public clients.
# Revoking a refresh token cascades to invalidate its associated access tokens.
# Revoked tokens are rejected by resource server checks immediately (via revocation/denylist table), not just after natural expiry.
# PHPUnit test coverage for: valid revocation, invalid/unknown token (still 200), foreign-token rejection, and cascading revocation.
